objective: Make a signed attestation status evidence-backed: promotion requires the attestation to name the published subject digest and to record the verification that was performed against the registry.
decision_supported: Is a workflow-written `signed` string sufficient release evidence, and if not, what has to be checked before a manifest may be promoted?
acceptance: A signed status without a subject digest and a verification record is not promotable.
The subject digest must equal image.registry_digest.
verification.result must be 'verified', with a reference and a verifier.
The workflow runs gh attestation verify against the pushed digest and refuses when the bundle does not cover it.
release_eligible cannot be true when attestation verification is unavailable.
The documentation names the residual trust assumptions and does not call a workflow-written string a signature.
Tests cover an absent attestation, a mismatched digest, an unverified result, a missing reference or verifier, and a valid fixture.
evidence: Before the change record_attestation wrote {status, recorded_at} and promotion_reasons accepted any signed or verified string.
After the change recording signed with no evidence leaves release_eligible false with two named reasons.
A bundle naming a different digest exits 1 and writes no verification file; a matching bundle writes result=verified with the attested digests.
The end-to-end path: record_attestation with the verified record produces promotion_reasons () and release_eligible true.
stop_conditions: gh attestation verify is unavailable in the runner image; the step fails closed rather than marking the manifest signed.
The attestation store returns a bundle for a different identity; the subject digest check does not cover identity, which the documentation states as a residual trust.
risks_and_fallbacks: A release now needs the attestation to be readable immediately after the push; a registry propagation delay would fail the run rather than promote unverified, which is the intended direction.
The verifier name is recorded as the command that ran, so a future change to how verification is done is visible in the manifest.
